officials.name: Jay Patterson
officials.bio: Jay Patterson serves as a Council Member for Place 3 on the City Council.

officials.name: Lynn Beard
officials.bio: Lynn Beard serves as a City Council Member for Place 2. He is the General Manager of Abilene Aero, Inc. and a retired Lieutenant from the Abilene Police Department. Beard is actively involved in various community activities, including serving as an Elder at Beltway Park Church and as President of the Executive Board of Directors for the Regional Victims’ Crisis Center.

officials.name: Miguel Espinoza
officials.bio: Miguel Espinoza is a Council Member for Place 5 on the City Council. He is a certified public accountant with a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration and a Masters of Accountancy from Abilene Christian University. Born and raised in Abilene, he is involved in various community activities.

officials.name: Shane Price
officials.bio: Shane Price serves as a Council Member for Place 1. He holds a B.S. in Computer Science from Abilene Christian University and has a professional background as a Bookstore Manager and Vice President of Development. A lifelong resident of Abilene, he is involved in community activities and has four children with his spouse, Carmen.

officials.name: Travis Craver
officials.bio: Travis Craver serves as Council Member - Place 6 and is the Executive Director of Mentoring Alliance. He holds degrees from Hardin-Simmons University and Baylor University. In his personal life, he enjoys active outdoor activities, reading, and spending time with his family.

officials.name: Weldon W. Hurt
officials.bio: Weldon W. Hurt is the Mayor of Abilene. He is the President of Pest Patrol, a locally owned and operated business for 25 years, and holds an Associates Degree from Western Texas College. He is actively involved in the community, serving as a current board member for the Abilene Convention and Visitors Bureau and previously on several other local boards.

officials.name: Jim Ross
officials.bio: Mayor Jim Ross was elected to the office of Mayor at the City of Arlington in June 2021. Jim has spent decades serving his community and his country. As a proud resident of Arlington for forty years, he has witnessed the growth and growing pains this community has endured.

officials.bio: Jacob Powell was first elected the District 5 Council Member in December 2020. He moved to Baytown in 2008 for an internship and returned in 2011 after graduating from Auburn University with a bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering. He currently serves on the Board of Directors for the Goose Creek CISD Education Foundation and CASA, and is employed as a Power Distribution Engineer at Covestro.

officials.name: James Franco
officials.address: Baytown City Hall Council Chamber 2401 Market Street Baytown, TX 77520
officials.bio: Born and raised in Baytown, James Franco is a product of Goose Creek CISD and Lee College. He is a partner and Chief Financial Officer in a construction firm, bringing extensive experience in project management and development. His top priorities include ensuring citizens' needs are met and leaving a positive impact for future generations.

officials.name: Ken Griffith
officials.address: Baytown City Hall Council Chamber 2401 Market Street Baytown, TX 77520
officials.bio: Kenrick Griffith is a 40-year resident of Baytown and a graduate of Robert E. Lee High School. He has a background in private security, working his way up to Director of Security for Home Depot distribution center, and currently serves as site supervisor for Shell Federal Credit Union. Kenrick is actively involved in the community, having coached youth football and volunteered with various charities and organizations.

officials.name: Laura Alvarado
officials.address: Baytown City Hall Council Chamber 2401 Market Street Baytown, TX 77520
officials.bio: Laura Alvarado was first elected the District 1 Council Member in November 2016, with her current term expiring November 2025. She serves as the Community Systems Manager for First3Years, focusing on developing integrated community systems in Baytown, and previously held a role as Senior Director of Operations for the National Diversity Council. Alvarado is also actively involved in various community boards and committees, including the Houston Galveston Area Council and the Municipal Development District.

officials.name: Sarah Graham
officials.address: Baytown City Hall Council Chamber 2401 Market Street Baytown, TX 77520
officials.bio: Sarah Graham is a lifelong resident of Baytown and the current Science Content Specialist at Robert E. Lee High School. She holds a Bachelor of Science in Biology and a Masters of Ed in Educational Administration. Graham is active in the Baytown community, volunteering through her church and serving on various committees.

officials.name: Charles Johnson
officials.address: Baytown City Hall Council Chamber 2401 Market Street Baytown, TX 77520
officials.bio: Charles Johnson is a lifelong resident of Baytown with a deep-rooted passion for service, leadership, and community development. He served two consecutive terms on the Baytown City Council from 2017 to 2022 and currently serves on numerous community boards. Professionally, he is a commercial and residential real estate agent.

officials.name: Chris Durio
officials.bio: Chris Durio is married to Gwendolyn Durio and has two children and four grandchildren. He is a 1980 graduate of Hebert High School, served in the U.S. Navy, and retired as a Captain from the Beaumont Fire Department after 31 years of service.

officials.bio: Albert “AJ” Turner is a lifelong native of Beaumont, Texas, and a devoted father. He has served as a leader in the community and as a City Councilmember At-Large for the City of Beaumont since May 2021. He graduated with Honors from Central High School and holds a Bachelor of Science in Sociology from Wiley College.

officials.name: Roy West
officials.bio: Roy West is a proud, lifelong Texan, born and raised in Beaumont. He graduated from Lamar University and Southern Methodist University, and has over 30 years of experience as a business owner. Elected Mayor of the City of Beaumont in May 2023, he is committed to creating a thriving, united Beaumont.

officials.name: John Cowen, Jr.
officials.bio: Honorable Mayor John Cowen, Jr. is a distinguished public servant and a 6th generation Brownsvillian. Elected as Mayor in 2023, he leads key initiatives to enhance the city's economy, infrastructure, quality of life, and long-term development.

officials.name: Alexis Frezza
officials.bio: Alexis Frezza, City Council Place 1, has lived in Central Texas for nearly 40 years and returned to Cedar Park to raise her children. She holds a Bachelor's degree from Texas State University and has over a decade of experience serving on nonprofit boards. Frezza is committed to preserving community values and shaping a bright future for Cedar Park residents.

officials.name: Anne Duffy
officials.bio: Anne K. Duffy was elected to a fifth term to serve on Place 3 of the Cedar Park City Council in May 2025. She was elected to her first term for Place 3 in 2017, her second term for Place 3 in 2019, her third term for Place 3 in 2021, her fourth term in 2023,and served as Mayor Pro Tem from May 2018 until May 2019 and again serving as Mayor Pro Tem from April 2023 to May 2024. She is a native of Montana but has lived in Cedar Park since August 1999.

officials.name: Darron Jurajda
officials.bio: Darron Jurajda was born and raised in Central Texas, where he met his wife, Inger, while attending high school in Austin. Both later graduated from The University of Texas at Austin. After earning a Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering, Darron and Inger chose Cedar Park as the place to build their life together.

officials.name: Jim Penniman-Morin
officials.bio: Jim Penniman-Morin was reelected Mayor of Cedar Park in May 2026for his third term. He was previously elected to serve on Place 1 of the Cedar Park City Council in 2021. Mayor Jim is proud to play a role in continuing the smart and successful growth of our city as a thriving, safe and inclusive community.

officials.name: Kevin Harris
officials.bio: Kevin Harris was re-elected to his third term on Place Five of the Cedar Park City Council in May 2025, having served since 2021. A Cedar Park resident since 1997, he has a long history of community involvement, including serving on the Community Development board and Planning and Zoning Commission. He is also a U.S. Army Reserve Lieutenant Colonel (Ret.) and a business owner.

officials.name: Michael Endres
officials.bio: Michael Endres was elected to the Cedar Park City Council in 2026. He has served in law enforcement for over 14 years, currently as a Patrol Lieutenant for downtown Austin, and is active in community service. Michael earned his MBA and is committed to improving the quality of life for Cedar Park residents.

officials.name: Shweta Padmanabha
officials.bio: Elected to Place Six of the Cedar Park City Council in May 2026, Shweta Padmanabha is a long-time Cedar Park resident, community advocate, and proud mother of two. Having called Cedar Park home for over 15 years, she is deeply grateful for the opportunities and support the community provided her family during an important chapter of their lives. Shweta is a graduate of the Cedar Park Leadership Academy and has been actively involved in civic and community service for several years.

officials.name: Donetta Roberts
officials.bio: Donetta Roberts is a native Texan who has proudly called Cibolo home since 2004. A graduate of Calallen High School in Corpus Christi, she later pursued higher education at the University of Texas at San Antonio, where she earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science.

officials.name: Norma Sanchez-Stephens
officials.bio: Norma Sanchez-Stephens is a native Texan and a longtime resident of the Texas Tri-County area, holding a Bachelor's Degree in Banking and Finance. After a successful career in the mortgage industry, she dedicated time to her family and volunteered with the National Guard Unit's Family Readiness Group. She is honored to represent At-Large Place 5 and the City of Cibolo, serving its residents.

officials.name: Summer-Marie Brown
officials.bio: Summer-Marie Brown was elected to the Cibolo City Council, representing At Large Place 7, in December 2025. She was born in Joplin, Missouri, and raised in the Netherlands as a military child, an experience that shaped her global perspective and deep respect for service. She served nine years as an enlisted Soldier in the United States Army before receiving a Direct Commission as an Active-duty Medical Service Officer, and her civilian career includes senior leadership roles in Human Resources.

officials.name: Jeff McGlothin
officials.bio: Jeff McGlothin was born in Milwaukie, Oregon, and holds degrees in Intelligence Technologies and Criminal Justice. He served in the Oregon Air National Guard as an intelligence analyst and later as an Intelligence Officer in the Air Force Reserve. After moving to Cibolo, Texas, in 2019, he was elected to City Council in 2023, advocating for small businesses and preserving Cibolo's small-town charm.

officials.name: Marissa-Ellen Patterson
officials.bio: Marissa-Ellen Patterson was elected to the Cibolo City Council in December 2025 and is honored to serve as the Place 3 Councilwoman. She is committed to advancing smart growth, public safety, fostering innovation, and championing transparent, community-centered governance.

officials.name: Katie Cunningham
officials.bio: Katie Cunningham was elected to the Cibolo City Council, representing District 4, in November 2021. With extensive experience in nonprofit organizations and city government, Katie has cultivated a deep passion for community service and a people-first approach. She is actively engaged in her community, regularly participating in block walks, attending neighborhood and community meetings, communicating with constituents via calls and texts, conducting ride-alongs with city departments, organizing and contributing to community clean-up efforts, and collaborating with numerous outstanding organizations throughout the Cibolo area.

officials.name: Kara Latimer
officials.bio: As mayor of Cibolo, Kara Latimer is committed to leadership grounded in professionalism, stability, and respect. Having raised her family and built her business in Cibolo, she works to ensure the city thrives for current and future generations.

officials.name: Kevin Webb
officials.bio: Kevin Webb was elected in November of 2012 and has won re-election twice. Born and raised in Comal County, he graduated from New Braunfels High School and Texas A&M with a B.S. in Recreation, Parks, and Tourism. In office, Kevin has primarily focused on transportation and currently serves as the Vice Chairman of the Alamo Area Metropolitan Planning Organization (AAMPO).

officials.bio: Brian Wesley has proudly called the Dallas area home for more than 47 years. A dedicated public servant, he is committed to strengthening the DeSoto community through leadership, service, and meaningful community engagement.

officials.name: Crystal Chism
officials.address: 211 East Pleasant Run Road DeSoto, TX 75115
officials.bio: Crystal Chism proudly serves as the DeSoto City Councilmember for Place 6, having secured a resounding 62.86% of the vote in the May 1, 2021 election. She was recently re-elected for her second full term, in May 2024. Her journey in public service is a testament to her dedication to her constituents and her community.

officials.name: Debrah North
officials.address: 211 East Pleasant Run Road DeSoto, TX 75115
officials.bio: A Dallas native and DeSoto resident, Debrah North brings a diverse background in financial services, insurance, asset management, and technology. Her professional career spans roles with Fortune 500 companies, tech startups, and executive coaching engagements across the U.S., with a focus on leadership development and client relationship management. Debrah remains committed to advocating for economic opportunity, safe and vibrant neighborhoods, and quality of life where residents and local businesses feel welcomed, represented, and supported.

officials.name: Pierette Parker
officials.address: 211 East Pleasant Run Road DeSoto, TX 75115
officials.bio: Pierette Parker was elected to DeSoto City Council in the June 2023 Runoff election to serve for Place Two. A 20+ year DeSoto resident, she has served on many boards/committees, including as Park Board Chair on the DeSoto Parks and Recreations Development Board. She is also a trained Technology Business Analyst, Certified Community Association Manager, and Texas Licensed Realtor(R).

officials.name: Ken Waters
officials.address: 211 East Pleasant Run Road DeSoto, TX 75115
officials.bio: Ken Waters joined the DeSoto City Council on June 16, 2025, and has been a longtime resident committed to serving and improving the community. With a background in business administration, he has worked across various industries and is actively involved in numerous community organizations, including leadership roles in civic and emergency response teams.

officials.name: Letitia Hughes
officials.address: 211 East Pleasant Run Road DeSoto, TX 75115
officials.bio: Letitia Hughes was elected to DeSoto City Council February 2021 (Special Election) to serve an unexpired term for Place Seven. She was recently re-elected for a third term (her second full term), in May 2024. Letitia has been a resident of the City of DeSoto for over 20 years and is the owner of The Hughes Group Real Estate Services in DeSoto.

officials.name: Rachel L. Proctor
officials.address: 211 East Pleasant Run Road DeSoto, TX 75115
officials.bio: Learn more about Mayor Rachel Proctor. Explore her leadership vision and contributions to the DeSoto community, including a full biography of her personal and professional milestones.

officials.name: Dr. Josh Acevedo
officials.bio: Representative Josh Acevedo was born and raised in the Five Points neighborhood of Central El Paso and has dedicated his career to public service. A four-time graduate of UTEP, he previously served on the El Paso Independent School District Board of Trustees from 2019 to 2024 before being elected to the City Council.

officials.address: City Hall 310 N Main Street P.O. Box 591 Elgin, TX 78621

officials.name: Cecil Chambers
officials.bio: As Forney continues to grow, Cecil Chambers is committed to preserving the qualities that make the community a great place to live while planning for the future. As a Lieutenant with the Dallas Police Department for nearly 20 years, he is committed to ensuring public safety. He is married with three children, has lived in Forney since 2005, and previously served on the Forney Planning and Zoning Commission.

officials.name: Greg Helm
officials.hours: Monday - Thursday 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Closed Fridays
officials.bio: I am married to a wonderful woman, and we have two fantastic daughters. I graduated from UNT with a Logistics Management degree and have worked in the Supply Chain arena for over 20 years. I have most recently served as Vice Chairman of the Planning and Zoning Commission.

officials.name: James Traylor
officials.bio: James Traylor is a City Council Member for Place 1, committed to thoughtful, responsible growth, attracting entertainment and recreational developments, and supporting public safety. He has a background in multi-family development and property management and has been actively involved with the Forney Soccer Association.

officials.name: Jason Roberson
officials.hours: Monday - Thursday 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Closed Fridays
officials.bio: Jason Roberson was first elected to the Forney City Council in May 2021 and aims to continue building Forney's infrastructure, fostering an ethical environment, and supporting first responders. His professional background is in communications, working as a journalist, public relations executive, and ghostwriter.

officials.name: Jay Weatherford
officials.bio: Jay Weatherford serves on the Forney City Council, Place 3, with his term expiring in 2027. He is a retired CPA with a bachelor's degree in accounting, bringing extensive experience from private, non-profit, and public program administration. As a father and grandfather, his primary goals for Forney include ensuring family safety and fostering a family-friendly environment amidst the city's growth.

officials.name: Sarah Salgado
officials.bio: I’m a native Texan who has lived in Forney for over 15 years. My professional background is in education, with a Bachelor of Science in Special Education. I am married with four children and ran for city council to help Forney be its best for decades to come.

officials.name: Zahnd Schlensker
officials.bio: I am a native of Richardson, Texas. Forney has been my home for the last 19 years. I graduated from Austin College in Sherman, TX, and have worked in the Automobile Industry for 29 years. I have a son, Luke, who is engaged to my future daughter-in-law Janell.

officials.name: Ann Anderson
officials.bio: Council Member Ann Anderson was elected to the Frisco City Council in a special election held in January 2026 to represent Place 1. A longtime Frisco resident and small business owner, Ann has spent more than 20 years actively serving the Frisco community through civic leadership, nonprofit involvement, and volunteer service. She is the owner of Ann Anderson Insurance Agency and is married to Thor with two children.

officials.name: Brittany Colberg
officials.bio: Brittany Colberg is a dedicated community leader, business professional, and 26-year Frisco resident who has spent years serving the city through volunteer leadership, citizen engagement, and municipal governance. She brings a deep understanding of Frisco's growth, challenges, and opportunities, along with a commitment to thoughtful, transparent, and resident-focused leadership.

officials.name: Jared Elad
officials.bio: Elected to Frisco City Council : 2025 Current Term Expires : May 2028. Complete bio coming soon.

officials.name: Angelia Pelham
officials.bio: Angelia Pelham was elected to the Frisco City Council in June 2021 and currently serves as Deputy Mayor Pro Tem. She has a 35-year career as a Human Resources Executive, holding roles at companies like Walt Disney World, PepsiCo, and Cinemark Holdings. Pelham is also CEO of Real-Talk Executive Coaching & Development and is actively involved in community leadership, including the Linking Cultures of Frisco non-profit.

officials.name: Laura Rummel
officials.bio: Councilwoman Laura Rummel was elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2023, serving as Mayor Pro Tem and Council Member, Place 5. She has championed initiatives like increasing homestead tax exemptions, implementing the Senior Tax Freeze, and securing state funding for Grand Park. With over 20 years in consumer products and financial technology, she holds an Executive MBA from Southern Methodist University.

officials.name: Mark Hill
officials.bio: Mayor Mark Hill was elected in June 2026. He previously served on the Frisco Independent School District Board of Trustees and the Frisco Economic Development Corporation board. A corporate attorney and Managing Partner at Henry Hill, PLLC, he earned his law degree from St. Mary’s University and a BBA in Finance from Texas A&M University.

officials.name: Jimmy Tran
officials.bio: Jimmy Tran was elected to serve as the Garland City Council Member for District 1 in May 2026. A Garland resident of over 24 years, Jimmy is deeply committed to strengthening the community through responsive leadership, public safety and sustainable economic growth.

officials.name: Joe Thomas Jr.
officials.bio: Joe Thomas Jr., District 7 Council Member, was elected to his first term on the Garland City Council in May 2025. He retired from full-time work in 2026 to devote more time to the city he loves. As a Council member, he aims to improve city infrastructure and continue Garland’s economic growth.

officials.name: Margaret Lucht
officials.bio: Margaret Lucht, District 5 City Council member, was sworn in for her first term in 2022. A lifelong resident of District 5, she is a Certified Dental Technician and currently a human resources administrator. She is dedicated to improving District 5 and making Garland a safer, more enjoyable place to live, work, and play.

officials.name: Carissa Dutton
officials.office: Deputy Mayor Pro Tem, City Council Member
officials.bio: Carissa Dutton, District 6 Council Member, was elected in May 2023. A 30-year resident of Garland, her extensive community service began as a teenager and includes tornado clean-up efforts, earning her Garland's first-ever Make Your Mark award in 2020. By profession a caretaker, she dedicates her free time to organizations like Garland Overnight Warming Station (GLOWS) and the Garland Optimist Club.

officials.name: Chris Ott
officials.office: Mayor Pro Tem, City Council Member
officials.bio: Chris Ott, District 8 Council Member, was elected to his first term in May 2023 and serves as Mayor Pro Tem. He is an advocate for the business community, open spaces, and the arts, with a history of civic involvement including 13 years on the City's Plan Commission. Chris is also a small business owner, having founded Rotary Performance in Garland in 1988.

officials.name: Dylan Hedrick
officials.bio: After serving three consecutive terms as District 7 Council member, Dylan Hedrick was elected to his first term as Garland Mayor in June of 2025. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering and a Masters of Business Administration from Rice University. As mayor, Dylan hopes to combine his engineering background with his business expertise to help rebuild city infrastructure, further Garland's economic development, and promote a better quality of life.

officials.bio: Elected to Place 5 in 2008, Chris Coy's term expires in 2026. A Grapevine resident since 1989, he is the Vice President of Finance for Authentix and holds an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

officials.name: Duff O'Dell
officials.bio: Duff O'Dell was elected to Place 6 in 2014, with her term expiring in 2026. A Grapevine resident since 1985, she is married to Patrick O'Dell and is retired from Delta Air Lines and Premier Bank Texas.

officials.name: Leon Leal
officials.bio: Leon Leal has been a proud Grapevine resident since 1992, dedicating decades to serving the community through civic, educational, and nonprofit organizations, including nine years on the Grapevine-Colleyville Board of Trustees. He is a graduate of the University of Oklahoma, owner of Abba Staffing & Consulting Inc. and Abba Investment LLC, and is committed to preserving Grapevine's quality of life.

officials.name: Sean Shope
officials.bio: A lifelong Grapevine resident, Sean Shope was elected to City Council Place 4 in 2025, with his term expiring in 2028. He brings over 30 years of professional experience in banking and finance to his community service, and he and his wife, Paula, are proud parents and grandparents.

officials.name: Sharron Rogers
officials.bio: Sharron Rogers was elected to Place 2 in 1985, with her current term expiring in 2027. She has been a Grapevine resident since 1975, retired from American Airlines after 21 years of service, and is a past Vice President for Spencer Engineering, Inc.

officials.name: Paul Slechta
officials.office: Mayor Pro Tem, City Council Member
officials.bio: Paul Slechta was elected to Place 1 in November 2015 and Mayor Pro Tem in May 2025, with his term expiring in May 2027. A Grapevine resident since 1990 and a graduate of North Carolina State University, he owns Panda Embroidery in Grapevine and is married to Tiffany with two children, Katelyn and Tucker.

officials.name: William D. Tate
officials.bio: Born and raised in Grapevine, William D. Tate has a law practice and title company in the city. He holds a Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting from North Texas State University and a Doctor of Jurisprudence from the University of Houston. He is married to Betty Tate and they have five daughters.

A U.S. Army veteran, he is also a community leader involved in youth sports and mentorship programs.

officials.bio: Andrew has been a proud resident of Little Elm for several years and is a dedicated Christian and father to his daughter and son. In addition to serving his constituents, Andrew is a senior operations consultant in the mortgage servicing industry. His main focus is to enhance Little Elm's future by attracting jobs, entertainment, dining, and recreational opportunities while addressing the town's geographical and commuting challenges to bring the community closer together.

officials.name: Idalia Maria Amaya
officials.address: 100 W. Eldorado Parkway Little Elm, Texas 75068
officials.bio: Councilmember Idalia Maria Amaya was elected to the Little Elm Town Council in 2025. She is a dedicated public servant and proud native of Little Elm, with over 15 years of experience in social work, education, nonprofit leadership, and community development. She holds a Bachelor of Science from the University of Texas at Austin and dual master's degrees from Columbia University.

officials.name: Jamell T. Johnson
officials.address: 100 W. Eldorado Parkway Little Elm, Texas 75068
officials.bio: Council Member Jamell T. Johnson has lived in Little Elm since 2019, relocating from Indiana with his family. He earned a B.S. in Criminology and an M.J. in Business Law, served in the military for ten years, and was elected as the youngest Council Member in the Town's history.

officials.name: Ken Eaken
officials.address: 100 W. Eldorado Parkway Little Elm, Texas 75068
officials.bio: Prior to his election to the Town Council in May 2024, Ken has been actively engaged in the community, having been appointed by the Town Council to the Little Elm Economic Development Corporation Board of Directors in 2018 and serving as its President since 2020. He is a graduate of all the Towns Academies, Citizens, Police and Fire, volunteering in both Citizens on Patrol and Box 620 supporting the Fire Department. He believes his background and experience will assist in the future direction of the Town of Little Elm and is grateful for this opportunity to continue his service to the community.

officials.name: Tony Singh
officials.address: 100 W. Eldorado Parkway Little Elm, Texas 75068
officials.bio: Tony Singh, born in India, moved to the U.S. in 2003 to pursue graduate degrees in Electrical Engineering and an MBA from the University of Texas at Arlington. He and his wife, Crystal, have resided in Little Elm's District 2 since 2011, where he works in the telecom industry. Tony is dedicated to community service, volunteering with local police and fire departments, and previously serving on the Planning & Zoning Commission.

officials.name: Michel Hambrick
officials.address: 100 W. Eldorado Parkway Little Elm, Texas 75068
officials.hours: Monday-Thursday 7:30 a.m.-5:30 p.m. Friday 7:30 a.m.-11:30 a.m.
officials.bio: Michel has lived in Little Elm since October 2005 with her husband Kevin and daughter McKaylah. A small business owner since 2015, she has served on numerous community boards including the Little Elm Friends of the Library and the Little Elm Economic Development Corporation.

officials.name: Curtis J. Cornelious
officials.address: 100 W. Eldorado Parkway Little Elm, Texas 75068
officials.bio: Mayor Curtis J. Cornelious has lived in Little Elm since October 2004, with his wife of over 19 great years, Charlet, and their three children Stephanie, Christian, and Collyn. He has a double degree in Chemistry and Agriculture from the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff. He has always been involved in his community through different organizations, including coaching football and basketball, Boy Scouts, and his church, where he served as a Deacon. He served two terms on Town Council representing District 3, two terms as an at-large representative and served five years as Mayor Pro Tem. He also served as a Board Director for the Economic Development Corporation for four years. He served(s) on numerous boards around the county. Mayor Cornelious is a proud member of Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc.

officials.name: Juan Fresquez
officials.bio: Juan Fresquez Jr., MBA, is a distinguished figure in healthcare leadership and civic engagement, currently serving as President of Methodist Mansfield Medical Center. With over three decades of experience in acute care hospital management, he has honed expertise in operations, leadership, and quality improvement. In May 2024, he was sworn in as Mansfield City Councilman Place 4, committed to improving the quality of life for all residents.

officials.name: Tamera Bounds
officials.bio: Tamera J. Bounds was elected to the Mansfield City Council, Place 2, in 2020, having previously served on the Planning & Zoning Commission. A 44-year resident of Mansfield, she has volunteered with numerous local organizations and is a Texas Municipal League Lifetime Fellow. After a 30-year career in physical therapy, she recently retired.

officials.name: Todd Simmons
officials.bio: Todd Simmons was elected to Mansfield City Council Place 5 in June 2025 and previously chaired the Mansfield Economic Development Corporation Board. He holds degrees in Political Science, Accounting, and Business Administration, and currently owns Simmons Wealth Management. Todd is an active volunteer in the community, serving with organizations like the Kiwanis Club, Walnut Ridge Baptist church, and various Mansfield ISD committees.

officials.name: Todd Tonore
officials.bio: Mansfield businessman Todd Tonore was elected to City Council Place 6 in November 2020 and has served as Mayor Pro Tem since 2021. He is the founder and chief executive officer of several businesses in the city and holds a degree in business administration from Northeast Louisiana University. He and his wife Tonyia have been married for 34 years and have four daughters and seven wonderful grandchildren.

officials.name: Michael Evans
officials.bio: Reverend Dr. Michael A. Evans, Sr. was elected Mayor of the City of Mansfield, Texas, in December 2020. He is also the proud pastor of the Bethlehem Baptist Church, where he has served for over 30 years. Mayor Evans holds a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Texas at Arlington, a Master of Divinity from Texas Christian University, and a Doctor of Ministry from Baylor University.

officials.name: Aaron Styron
officials.bio: Councilmember Aaron Styron is a lifelong resident of Pasadena and a proud graduate of Sam Rayburn High School. He is a Captain for a major airline and the founder of a Pasadena-based real estate company. As the elected representative for District H, he is focused on promoting fiscal responsibility, supporting public safety, and ensuring responsive representation.

officials.name: Bianca Valerio
officials.bio: In 2021, Bianca Valerio committed to run for City Council District B and represent her community, becoming the first Hispanic Woman elected to Pasadena's Council. She was re-elected for a second term in 2023. She is committed to supporting first responders, public safety, infrastructure improvements, and community programs.

officials.name: Carlos Heredia Sr.
officials.bio: Carlos Heredia has built a successful career in civil engineering since 2003, contributing to a wide range of infrastructure and development projects across the region. An accomplished amateur boxer, he captured titles in the Copper Gloves, Silver Gloves, Golden Gloves, and the 1996 Junior Olympics. Although he excelled in the ring, Carlos chose to shift his focus toward his career and family life in Pasadena, Texas, where he is a devoted father to three boys and a daughter who proudly served in the U.S. National Guard.

officials.name: Emmanuel Guerrero
officials.bio: Councilman Emmanuel Guerrero was born in Pasadena, Texas, in 1996, and is a first-generation college graduate from the University of Houston's Bauer Business School. He holds double Bachelor of Business Administration degrees in Finance and Marketing, which he completed in three years. He currently works for a consulting firm specializing in disaster relief and emergency response, serving as the youngest manager in the firm's history.

officials.name: Johnny Fusilier Jr.
officials.bio: Born and raised in Pasadena, Johnny Fusilier Jr. is a Council Member for District G, dedicated to community service and development. He holds a master's degree, works as a physical education teacher in Pasadena ISD, and is actively involved in local nonprofits and his church. He is a proud father of five children who all attend Pasadena schools.

officials.name: Jonathan Estrada
officials.bio: Councilmember Jonathan Estrada was born and raised in Pasadena, Texas, and is a proud product of Pasadena ISD public schools. He worked for the City of Houston for ten years before being elected to City Council in June 2021, and has since been re-elected for additional terms, prioritizing constituent services and infrastructure improvements.

officials.name: Pat Van Houte
officials.bio: Councilmember Pat Van Houte was born in Syracuse, NY, and grew up in Cleveland, OH. She holds a BS in Psychology and an MA in Behavioral Sciences, and has lived in District D since 1980. Retired from the State of Texas, she previously served as a District D councilmember from 2009-2015, an at-large councilmember from 2015-2017, and returned to represent District D in 2021.

officials.name: Thomas Schoenbein
officials.bio: Mayor Thomas Schoenbein was sworn in as Mayor of Pasadena on July 1, 2025, and has been a proud resident of the community for more than 50 years. He and his wife, Bonnie, are the parents of two children and the grandparents of three grandchildren. Mayor Schoenbein brings deep experience, steady leadership, and a clear vision for Pasadena’s future.

officials.name: Ben Long
officials.bio: Ben Long has called Princeton home since 2020, is married with three children, and has over 25 years of construction experience. He is dedicated to facilitating growth and enhancing the quality of life for his community.

officials.name: Bryan Washington
officials.bio: Bryan Washington, Mayor Pro Tem and Council Member, Place 3, has deep roots in Princeton, moving there in 2008. He is known for his commitment to youth sports, community outreach, and supporting local businesses, including co-founding The Jym—Princeton. Now in his second term on City Council, he focuses on enhancing local parks, business growth, and job opportunities, having been appointed Mayor Pro Tem in 2025.

officials.name: Carolyn David-Graves
officials.bio: Carolyn David-Graves grew up in the Caribbean and moved to Texas in 2015, choosing Princeton for her family's home. Committed to the city's growth, she joined the City Council to make a positive difference. She holds a Masters Degree in Public Administration and Mental Health Counseling and works as a Clinical Research Quality & Regulatory Specialist.

officials.name: Cristina Todd
officials.bio: Cristina Todd made Princeton her home in 2016 with her husband, Jake, and their pets. She has a lifelong commitment to community service, fostered by Rotary's principle of "Service Above Self," and has been actively involved with Rotary for over 20 years. Cristina holds a Bachelor of Science and a Master's degree from the University of North Texas and has nearly two decades of experience in Special Education.

officials.name: Jaisen Rutledge
officials.bio: Jaisen Rutledge is committed to thoughtful leadership, responsible governance, and serving the residents of Princeton with integrity, transparency, and accountability. A proud Princeton resident, he and his wife are raising their three sons in the community. Before being elected to City Council, Jaisen served in several key leadership roles, including as the first African American Chair of the Princeton Community Development Corporation.

officials.name: Steven Deffibaugh
officials.bio: Steven Deffibaugh was born in Borger, Texas, was married to his wife Judy for 46 years, and has one son and two grandkids. Some of his career highlights include serving in the Marine Corps, being a police officer for both the Van Alstyne and McKinney Police Departments, and being Collin County Fire Marshal, to name a few. His background includes serving two terms as Mayor for the City of Princeton; he currently serves as Mayor Pro Tempore and has been on the City Council since May of 2010.

officials.name: Terrance Johnson
officials.bio: Terrance Johnson is a Dallas, Texas, native and alumnus of Woodrow Wilson High School, who pursued a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration at Texas A&M University–Commerce. He relocated to Collin County in 2013 to launch a faith-based youth organization and later served as the first African American Board Chair for the Princeton Economic Development Corporation. Married with two daughters, he is deeply invested in policies enhancing quality of life and educational opportunities for Princeton families.

Rockwall County is a unique place with a great quality of life, and I plan to work very hard to maintain that.

officials.name: Dana Macalik
officials.address: 101 East Rusk Street Suite 202 Rockwall , TX 75087
officials.bio: Dana K Cullins Macalik was elected to the Rockwall County Commissioners Court (Precinct 2) in November 2022, effective January 1, 2023. A 5th-generation Rockwall County resident, she graduated from Rockwall High School in 1980 and Sam Houston State University. She previously served on the Rockwall City Council from 2017-2022.

He earned his J.D. and MBA degrees from the University of Notre Dame in 1981. Lorne is the Rockwall County Commissioner for Precinct 3, having previously served two terms as Mayor of Heath and four terms on the Heath City Council.

officials.name: Amanda J. Barta
officials.bio: Councilor Barta was elected to serve the City of Rosenberg on May 2, 2026 as Councilor At Large, Position 2. She served the residents of the City of Rosenberg in multiple leadership roles over six years, including as Council Member for District 4 and Mayor Pro-Tem.

officials.name: Richard Olson
officials.bio: Richard Olson was first elected to Rosenberg City Council District 4 in 2018, At Large, Position 1 in a runoff election on June 15, 2024 and At Large, Position 1 on May 2, 2026.

officials.name: George A. Zepeda
officials.bio: Councilor George Zepeda was elected to the office of City Councilor, District 4 in May 2022, re-elected on May 4, 2024, and again on May 2, 2026.

officials.name: Scott Peterson
officials.bio: Councilor Peterson is a licensed Customs Broker with 20 years experience working privately to assist importers with Customs clearance, import compliance, and timely payment of duty.

officials.name: Steven DeGregorio
officials.bio: Steve DeGregorio was first elected to Rosenberg City Council District 2 in 2018, re-elected in a runoff election held on June 15, 2024, and again on May 2, 2026.

officials.name: Felix Vargas, Jr.
officials.bio: Felix was first elected to District 1 in May 2024 and again on May 2, 2026, and was appointed Mayor Pro Tem on July 7, 2026. A Rosenberg, Texas native, he is a Foster High School graduate and earned an associate degree in computer electronics. With 17 years of experience in oil and gas, Felix is now self-employed, running Vargas Removal Service.

officials.name: William Benton
officials.bio: William Benton was first elected to Rosenberg City Council in 2011 and became Mayor in 2017, re-elected multiple times. He is a self-employed business owner with an Associate's and Bachelor's Degree. Mayor Benton is active in several community service organizations.

officials.name: Dr. Mark E. Davis
officials.bio: Councilmember Mark Davis has served on City Council since 2016, and he and his family have resided in Schertz since 2007. He retired from the United States Air Force as a Chief Master Sergeant in July 2009 and currently serves as the Chief of Information Protection for the 502d Air Base Wing at Joint Base San Antonio.

officials.name: Dr. Robert L. Sheridan III
officials.bio: Robert L Sheridan III is a retired federal contracting professional with more than 17 years of Department of Defense acquisition experience. He most recently served as a Division Chief with the U.S. Army’s 410th Contracting Support Brigade. He currently serves as a Councilmember for the City of Schertz, Texas, focusing on strengthening infrastructure, supporting economic growth, and delivering measurable results.

officials.name: Sarah Dietz
officials.bio: Born and raised in Arizona, Sarah Dietz received a bachelor's degree from Northern Arizona University. As a former military spouse, she spent 14 years supporting military families and later taught in the Schertz-Cibolo-Universal City Independent School District. Today, she is a full-time Realtor specializing in the Schertz/Cibolo areas and serves as President of the Women’s Council of Realtors Hill Country, deeply invested in serving her community.

officials.name: Michelle Watson
officials.bio: Councilwoman Michelle Watson was sworn into office to serve her first term in the Place 2 Council seat on Tuesday, January 17. Ms. Watson is a native Texan and a longtime resident of the Texas Tri-County area. Although this is Councilwoman Watson’s first elected position, she has been an active part of the South Texas Community.

officials.name: Rick Miller
officials.bio: Council Member D. F. “Rick” Miller is a retired U.S. Navy Captain and Naval Aviator, having served 30 years and commanded multiple units. He is the founder and President of TREVANIONGROUP, LLC, and currently serves on the Board of Directors for Impact A Hero and The Warriors Refuge.

officials.name: Robert Boettcher
officials.bio: Council Member Robert "Rob" Boettcher was elected to Sugar Land City Council as the At-Large Position 2 representative in June 2025. A Sugar Land resident since 2014, Rob and his family chose to make the city their home because of its exceptional quality of life, strong neighborhoods, and family-friendly community. Rob brings more than a decade of engineering experience in the energy industry and currently serves as a Senior Engineer with Schlumberger.

officials.name: Sanjay Singhal
officials.bio: Sanjay Singhal was elected to represent District 2 on the Sugar Land City Council in June 2025. He led in both the general and runoff elections with broad support across all neighborhoods and communities to deliver transparent governance and balanced growth for our city. Before joining City Council, Sanjay was an active community leader in Sugar Land.

officials.name: Stewart Jacobson
officials.bio: Stewart Jacobson was born in Chicago, Illinois and earned his JD from the University of Texas School of Law in 1984. He has been a Certified Financial Planner™ since 1988 and president of his own financial planning firm, Dearborn & Creggs, since 1989. Dearborn & Creggs is a traditional financial planning firm that also is deeply involved in the educator and municipal employee niche.

officials.name: Suzanne Whatley
officials.bio: Elected to a three-year term serving District One, Suzanne Whatley is a 27-year resident of Sugar Land, a small business owner of 19 years, a commercial property owner in District One, a mother of five, and an avid community leader in Sugar Land.

officials.name: Jim Vonderhaar
officials.bio: Jim Vonderhaar is a longtime Sugar Land resident, businessman, and dedicated community leader committed to smart growth, high quality of life, and a strong economy. With over 30 years in the energy sector and experience as a home care agency owner, he brings expertise in strategic planning, fiscal responsibility, and community service. A graduate of the University of Southern Mississippi, Jim is married with one son and two granddaughters.

officials.name: Carol McCutcheon
officials.bio: Mayor McCutcheon was elected to her first term as Mayor in 2025. She and her husband, Joe, have lived in Sugar Land since 1993. Mayor McCutcheon is known for her civic and community involvement, and has extensive experience as a reservoir engineer in the exploration and production of oil and gas.
